text:
sophie-sales: Quick ask — customer (LargeMed) wants a week-long POC using Redwood Private in their VPC. They want split-tunnel via customer VPN + PrivateLink to us for control-plane calls. Need checklist: which outbound ports must customer open from their NAT/Firewall? Also they asked about route priority and DNS resolution when using PrivateLink. Any quick docs I can send? :pray:

Tom: tom-eng: Short answer: control-plane (PrivateLink) uses HTTPS over TCP/443 to our interface endpoints. For dataplane (model inference) depending on deployment: if using Private (VPC) with our sidecar egress to internet you may need outbound 443 for model pulls and telemetry. If Dedicated in-customer, traffic stays internal. Can you confirm if they want egress to our hosted repo or pull from S3?

sophie-sales: They want all inference traffic to stay inside their VPC if possible. They said "no egress to public internet" in questionnaire. They asked about NAT and SNI inspection — will that break TLS handshake to our endpoint?

rajesh-se: If we do PrivateLink (interface endpoint) all TLS is native inside AWS with ENIs — SNI inspection might terminate TLS if TLS is intercepted. Customers must allow passthrough for our certs. Recommend adding our CNs to TLS passthrough or exempt the following SANs: *.redwood-inference.com and control-plane.<region>.privatelink.redwood.ai

elaine-infra: Firewall ports checklist I usually send:
- Outbound TCP 443 to privatelink endpoint ENI IPs
- Outbound TCP 22 (optional) for troubleshooting if they want bastion access
- DNS: allow UDP 53 (or TCP 53) to their resolver, and if using AWS Route53, enable resolution for privatelink private zones
- ICMP for path MTU? optional
Also for split-tunnel: ensure the default route for 0.0.0.0/0 still goes to client internet if customer wants browsing to stay local; specific prefixes for privatelink must route via ENI

rajesh-se: For route priority: interface endpoints create prefix lists (pl-xxxx) — attach to route table or SGs. If they have overlapping routes, ensure the route table with the privatelink ENI has higher priority (more specific). Example: add route for 10.12.0.0/16 -> eni-xxxx

sophie-sales: They also have an internal egress proxy that does SNI rewriting. Is there a tested fallback (can we offer a model variant hosted in their VPC with no egress?)

tom-eng: We can offer a fully private on-prem bundle (Paid enterprise option) that runs in their VPC, no egress. That's part of our Private package (requires licensing + SRE kickoff). For POC we can do PrivateLink + a model pulled from their private S3 (we can consume with IAM role). That avoids internet pulls.

rajesh-se: Quick snippet they can drop into their firewall allowlist:
```
# Allow to Redwood PrivateLink ENIs (example)
TCP 443 10.12.34.0/24  # privatelink ENI block
TCP 443 3.5.6.7        # if we give them explicit IP
UDP/TCP 53 <their-dns-ip>
```

Also add privatelink hosted zone to their Route53 resolver.

elaine-infra: For SAML/SSO and security questionnaire: we'll need to provide our SOC2 attestation, KMS integration details, and a short TODO: "we require customer to provide a role for S3 read access (arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/redwood-poc-s3)". I'll draft language.

sophie-sales: Pricing ask: they want to know delta for POC vs Dedicated reserved. Can someone send a one-pager with POC pricing (1 week, dev tier) and Dedicated uplift estimates?

tom-eng: I'll ping finance for a POC quote. For dedicated, typical uplift ~2.5x on hosted token price, or fixed commit. I'll DM exact numbers.

sophie-sales: Perfect. Can we also schedule a quick network runbook review with customer tomorrow 10am PST? I'll invite them.

infra-bot: Reminder: created ticket #INF-2024-789 for POC network review

sophie-sales: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll send the allowlist + draft questionnaire answers after tom shares pricing.
